title: Continuous coefficient sheaves preserve a finite lattice sum
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology and valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ with the subspace topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], continuous coefficient ring sheaves $A_T(U)=C(|U|,A)$ and $E_T(U)=C(|U|,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $r\geq0$, let $J$ be a nonempty finite set, and let $\Lambda_j\subseteq E^r$ admit $A$-bases that are also $E$-bases. Equip all lattices and $\Lambda=\sum_j\Lambda_j$ with their subspace topologies. The sum map $q:\bigoplus_j\Lambda_j\to\Lambda$ has a continuous $A$-linear right inverse, with the finite product topology on its domain. Consequently, for every topological space $Z$, the map $\bigoplus_j C(Z,\Lambda_j)\to C(Z,\Lambda)$ is surjective. On the pro-étale site of any scheme $S$, the sum of the submodule sheaves $U\mapsto C(|U|,\Lambda_j)$ inside $E_S^r$ is exactly $U\mapsto C(|U|,\Lambda)$. This sheaf is free of rank $r$ over $A_S$, and its inclusion becomes an isomorphism after extension to $E_S$.
